definitions.gloss: food simmered in sweetened soy sauce or sugar syrup; sweet-simmered
definitions.explanation: A Japanese cooking method where ingredients are slowly simmered in a sweet mixture of sugar, soy sauce, and mirin until glazed and tender. Common with small fish, chestnuts, and other ingredients.

examples.japanese: {鮎|あゆ}の{甘露煮|かんろに}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made sweetfish simmered in sweet soy.

examples.japanese: {栗|くり}の{甘露煮|かんろに}はおせちの{定番|ていばん}だ。
examples.english: Sweet-simmered chestnuts are a staple of New Year's dishes.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}が{作|つく}る{小魚|こざかな}の{甘露煮|かんろに}は、{骨|ほね}まで{柔|やわ}らかくて{絶品|ぜっぴん}だった。
examples.english: The sweet-simmered small fish my grandmother made were exquisite — tender right through to the bones.

notes:
A compound of {甘露|かんろ} (sweet nectar) and {煮|に} (simmering/cooking). A traditional Japanese preservation and cooking technique. The long, slow simmering in sweetened liquid gives the food a glossy, caramelized appearance and a sweet-savory flavor. Particularly associated with {鮎|あゆ} (sweetfish), {栗|くり} (chestnuts), and {佃煮|つくだに}-style small fish.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鮎|あゆ}の{甘露煮|かんろに}: candied sweetfish
- {栗|くり}の{甘露煮|かんろに}: candied chestnuts
- {甘露煮|かんろに}にする: to simmer in sweet syrup

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {佃煮|つくだに}: food simmered in soy and sugar — similar but typically uses stronger soy flavor and smaller pieces
- {煮付|につ}け: food simmered in seasoned broth — broader category, not necessarily sweet
- {砂糖漬|さとうづ}け: preserved in sugar — uses sugar without cooking
